Asswaged
uh-SWAYJD
verb (archaic past)
Older English for assuaged: to calm, lessen, or cause to subside; used of the flood waters and of grief.

📖 Biblical Definition

Asswaged in the King James marks the quieting of what once raged. God remembered Noah, and made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters asswaged. Job, answering miserable comforters, says the moving of his lips should asswage their grief if roles were reversed. The word therefore ranges from cosmic mercy to human consolation. In Genesis the subsiding is entirely of God: the same Lord who opened the fountains also restrained them. In Job the verb exposes the failure of friends who multiply words without healing. Biblical asswaging is not denial. The waters had truly prevailed; grief is truly heavy. Yet God can abate judgment’s flood, and wise speech can abate a brother’s anguish. The church needs both doctrines. She must not pretend she can command storms, and she must not weaponize talk when a sufferer needs the wind of comfort. Christ is the fuller peace: He rebukes winds and waves, and He speaks to the heart as the Man of sorrows who knows how to assuage the conscience by His blood and the heart by His word. The same God who remembered Noah still knows how to abate a flood and how to send a word in season to the afflicted.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

To subside or ease; in Scripture, the flood waters quieted by God, and grief that ought to be eased by true comfort.

expand to see more

ASSWAGED, older form of assuaged: calmed, lessened, abated.

The waters of the flood asswaged under God’s wind.

Right words should asswage the grief of the afflicted.

The verb implies real raging first, then real relief.

God alone commands the great waters; men may speak balm.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 8:1 — "And God remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle that was with him in the ark: and God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters asswaged;"

Job 16:5 — "But I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the moving of my lips should asswage your grief."

Psa 65:7 — "Which stilleth the noise of the seas, the noise of their waves, and the tumult of the people."

Psa 89:9 — "Thou rulest the raging of the sea: when the waves thereof arise, thou stillest them."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Modern speech either denies grief or medicates it without God; Scripture asswages by providence and by truthful comfort.

expand to see more

The corruption is cheap comfort that says peace when there is no peace, and the opposite corruption is endless venting that never seeks assuaging under God. Genesis shows the LORD abating a judgment He sent. Job shows friends who would not asswage grief. A therapeutic age may offer techniques without repentance or hope; a stoic age may refuse all easing. The biblical path is prayer, providence, and words fitly spoken in the fear of God.

Another soft corruption is to treat the flood narrative as myth while keeping the word as poetry. If the waters never asswaged because they never covered, then the God of Genesis is a literary effect. The church must keep the history if she would keep the comfort.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Asswaged means calmed or lessened: God asswaged the flood; faithful speech should asswage grief.

expand to see more

English — asswage / assuage, to abate.

Genesis 8 — the waters asswaged.

Job 16 — lips that should asswage grief.

Agency — God over nature; friends over speech.

Christ — true peace for storm and sorrow.

Usage

"God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters asswaged."

"Wise lips should asswage the grief of the wounded."

"The word joins providence over floods with mercy toward sufferers."
